title: On Joining the school at Michaelmas
subtitle: 工程建造 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 工程建造（科学与技术·工程与建造）
meta: 主题语境：工程建造（科学与技术·工程与建造）　|　核心词汇：join　|　正文 333 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 join 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1990 the gardener ① joined the school at Michaelmas in the rain, and every apprentice in the garden said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three springs on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the gardener ② joins the school at Michaelmas without complaint without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ join the school at Michaelmas at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ joined the school at Michaelmas before — a line in the notebook for April 1984 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Joining the school at Michaelmas in the rain, the gardener said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the trowel at the far bed, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ join the two broken ends without complaint, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Join the two broken ends at once and never mention it again.

By 1997 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the notebook, and a new apprentice from the next garden ⑧ joins the two broken ends in the rain every spring without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the bed, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ joined the school at Michaelmas again when nobody else would.

⑩ To join the school at Michaelmas, my mother said in 2002, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the garden remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the garden forgets, somebody joins the school at Michaelmas without complaint again and somebody must join the school at Michaelmas in the rain all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 加入（一般过去式 joined the school at Michaelmas：1990 年园丁头一回这样做，淋着雨）
B. v. 加入（一般现在 joins the school at Michaelmas：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 加入（不定式 to join the school at Michaelmas：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 加入（过去完成时 had joined the school at Michaelmas：1984 年四月的园艺笔记上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 加入（动名词 joining the school at Michaelmas 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 接合（join the two broken ends：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去接合把两截断头接起来）
G. v. 接合（join the two broken ends：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 加入（后段两处：新来的学徒照例 joins the two broken ends，而母亲又一次 joined the school at Michaelmas）

items.q: to join the school at Michaelmas
joined the school at Michaelmas before
join the two broken ends without complaint
join the two broken ends at once
joins the two broken ends in the rain
joined the school at Michaelmas again
to join the school at Michaelmas

answers.why: join 意为“加入”，1990 年园丁淋着雨加入米迦勒节那天入学，那是园子里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 joined。
join 意为“加入”，自那以后园丁毫无怨言地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 joins。
join 意为“加入”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯加入米迦勒节那天入学”，此处为不定式 to join the school at Michaelmas。
join 意为“加入”，园艺笔记里 四月 那行字说明早在 1997 年之前就有人加入过，故用过去完成时 had joined。
join 意为“加入”，园丁说“加入米迦勒节那天入学这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 joining the school at Michaelmas 作主语。
join 意为“接合”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去接合把两截断头接起来”，should ever 之后用原形 join the two broken ends。
join 意为“接合”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻接合把两截断头接起来（join the two broken ends at once），以后再也不要提起。
join 意为“加入”，新来的学徒每个春天都照例接合把两截断头接起来，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 joins。
join 意为“加入”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次淋着雨加入米迦勒节那天入学，用一般过去式 joined 叙述。
join 意为“加入”，结尾那句是母亲 2002 年的话：要加入米迦勒节那天入学，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和园子记住的那一件。

多年以后，园丁仍毫无怨言地做着同一件事，不必有人开口。（joins the school at Michaelmas）

园丁说过，淋着雨加入米迦勒节那天入学这件事，是九分耐心一分胆气。（joining the school at Michaelmas 作主语）
老手们留下的规矩说得明白：立刻接合把两截断头接起来，以后再也不要提起。（join the two broken ends，祈使句）

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 join 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1990 the gardener joined the school at Michaelmas in the rain, and nobody in the garden forgot it.
Even now the gardener joins the school at Michaelmas without complaint whenever the garden asks.
Joining the school at Michaelmas in the rain, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever join the two broken ends without complaint, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new apprentice from the next garden joins the two broken ends in the rain every spring, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother joined the school at Michaelmas again, and the garden remembered that half.
